items.title: New U-Boot flaws could enable stealthy firmware attacks
items.description: Six vulnerabilities in the widely used U-Boot bootloader have been discovered that could allow attackers to execute malicious code during device boot, potentially enabling stealthy firmware attacks that compromise security protections and install persistent malware. [...]

items.title: Jen Ellis: Connecting Cyber Community With Political Machinery
items.description: Security Pro File: On the heels of her recent honors as a Member of the Order of the British Empire (MBE), we take a look back at the events that shaped Jen Ellis' advocacy on behalf of security researchers.

items.title: Progress Urges ShareFile Admins to Shut Down Servers Over Credible Security Threat
items.description: Progress Software has issued an urgent advisory instructing customers running on-premises ShareFile Storage Zone Controllers to immediately power down the servers hosting these components, citing a “credible external security threat” against the platform. The notice, sent directly to customers’ inboxes, states that Progress has no current indication of unauthorized access to ShareFile accounts…

items.title: One WhatsApp Message Turns OpenClaw Into a Remote Access Tool for Hackers
items.description: Three high-severity vulnerabilities in OpenClaw, the open-source AI coding assistant with 381,000 GitHub stars, that allow attackers to achieve remote code execution through a single WhatsApp message. The flaws, confirmed exploitable on OpenClaw 2026.6.1, expose a structural weakness in how AI agents handle untrusted input from messaging channels. OpenClaw is a self-hosted AI assistant that […]…
